title: Forex Basics
summary: Understand currency pairs, pips, and spreads.
content:
Forex Basics: Currency Pairs, Pips, and Spreads

Type: Lesson

Duration: 5 minutes

Level: Beginner

Lesson Objective

By the end of this lesson, you will understand:

  • What currency pairs are
  • What pips mean in forex trading
  • How spreads affect your trades

1. What Are Currency Pairs?

Forex is the buying of one currency and selling another at the same time. Currencies are always traded in pairs because you are exchanging one currency for another.

Example: EUR/USD = 1.1000

This means EUR is the base currency and USD is the quote currency. The price tells us how much 1 Euro is worth in US Dollars.

Major Currency Pairs: EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY, USD/CHF, AUD/USD.

2. Understanding Buying and Selling

Buy (Long): You buy when you believe the first currency will increase in value.

Sell (Short): You sell when you believe the first currency will decrease in value.

3. What Is a Pip?

A pip means percentage in point and is the standard unit used to measure price movement in forex. For most currency pairs, 1 pip = 0.0001.

Example: EUR/USD moves from 1.1000 to 1.1001, which is 1 pip.

Traders use pips to measure profit, loss, risk, stop loss distance, and take profit targets.

4. What Is a Spread?

The spread is the difference between the buying price and selling price of a currency pair. Brokers show a bid price and an ask price.

Example: If the ask is 1.1002 and the bid is 1.1000, the spread is 2 pips. The broker earns this difference as a trading cost.

Key Points to Remember: Forex trades currencies in pairs, the first currency is the base currency, a pip measures price movement, most pairs move in 0.0001 increments, spread is the cost of entering a trade, and lower spreads usually mean lower trading costs.

Quick Practice Questions

  1. In EUR/USD, what currency are you buying when you click Buy? Answer: Euro.
  2. If EUR/USD moves from 1.2000 to 1.2050, how many pips did it move? Answer: 50 pips.
  3. If the spread is 3 pips, is that a trading cost? Answer: Yes.

title: Market Hours
summary: Learn when the major Forex sessions are open.
content:
Market Hours: Forex Sessions and Best Times to Trade

Type: Lesson

Duration: 4 minutes

Level: Beginner

Lesson Objective

By the end of this lesson, you will understand:

  • When the Forex market opens
  • The four major Forex trading sessions
  • The best times to trade

1. Forex Market Opening Hours

The Forex market is open 24 hours a day, 5 days a week because different financial centers around the world open at different times. The major Forex centers are Sydney, Tokyo, London, and New York. When one market closes, another one opens.

2. The Four Major Forex Sessions

1. Sydney Session

Time: 11:00 PM to 8:00 AM

Characteristics: lower volatility and good for Australian and New Zealand pairs.

2. Tokyo Session

Time: 1:00 AM to 10:00 AM

Characteristics: moderate movement and focus on Asian currencies.

3. London Session

Time: 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM

Characteristics: high volume and strong price movement.

4. New York Session

Time: 2:00 PM to 11:00 PM

Characteristics: high volatility and many economic news events.

3. The Best Trading Time

The strongest market movements usually happen when two sessions overlap. The London and New York overlap is one of the best periods because it offers high liquidity, more buyers and sellers, larger price movements, and often tighter spreads.

4. Why Market Hours Matter

Trading during the right session helps you find better opportunities, avoid slow markets, understand volatility, and choose better strategies. Beginners often avoid very quiet hours because movement can be slow.

Quick Review Questions

  1. How many days per week is Forex open? Answer: 5 days.
  2. Which session has the highest trading volume? Answer: London.
  3. What overlap is often considered best for trading? Answer: London and New York.

Key Takeaways: Forex runs 24 hours because markets open around the world, the four main sessions are Sydney, Tokyo, London, and New York, and session overlaps can provide the best trading opportunities.

title: Major Pairs
summary: Explore USD, EUR, JPY, and GBP currency pairs.
content:
Major Pairs: USD, EUR, JPY, and GBP

Type: Lesson

Duration: 5 minutes

Level: Beginner

Lesson Objective

By the end of this lesson, you will understand:

  • What major currency pairs are
  • The importance of USD, EUR, JPY, and GBP
  • The characteristics of popular Forex pairs

1. What Are Major Currency Pairs?

Major currency pairs are the most traded currency pairs in the Forex market. They always include the US Dollar because it is the most traded currency in the world.

Major pairs usually have high liquidity, lower spreads, large trading volume, and many opportunities.

2. The US Dollar

The US Dollar is involved in most Forex transactions. Examples include EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY, USD/CHF, AUD/USD, and USD/CAD.

It is important because the US economy is huge, many commodities are priced in dollars, and US economic news strongly moves the market.

3. EUR/USD

EUR/USD is the most traded pair in the world. It is very liquid, usually has low spreads, and is often recommended for beginners.

4. GBP/USD

GBP/USD is also called Cable. It often moves more aggressively than EUR/USD and can offer larger opportunities, but also more risk.

5. USD/JPY

USD/JPY is active during the Tokyo session and often reacts to Japanese economic news. It can also be influenced by risk sentiment.

6. Other Popular Major Pairs

USD/CHF is linked to the Swiss Franc and is often seen as a safe-haven currency. AUD/USD is influenced by commodities and Asian market activity. USD/CAD is affected by oil prices and North American trading.

7. Which Pair Should Beginners Start With?

Many beginners start with EUR/USD because it is easy to analyze, highly liquid, and often has lower spreads. Other good choices include GBP/USD and USD/JPY.

Quick Review Questions

  1. What currency appears in most major Forex pairs? Answer: USD.
  2. What is the most traded Forex pair? Answer: EUR/USD.
  3. Which pair is known for larger moves and higher volatility? Answer: GBP/USD.

Key Takeaways: Major pairs are the most traded Forex pairs, the US Dollar is the most important currency, EUR/USD is popular for beginners, and each pair behaves differently depending on economic news and session activity.

title: Risk Management
summary: Use stop losses and position sizing to protect capital.
content:
Risk Management: Protecting Your Capital

Type: Lesson

Duration: 6 minutes

Level: Intermediate

Lesson Objective

By the end of this lesson, you will understand:

  • Why risk management matters
  • How stop losses work
  • How to size positions safely

1. Why Risk Management Matters

Risk management helps protect your trading capital and keeps emotions under control. Even strong strategies can fail without proper risk control.

2. Stop Losses

A stop loss is an order that closes a trade if the market moves against you. It helps limit losses and keeps a trade from becoming emotionally hard to manage.

3. Position Sizing

Position sizing means choosing how much to risk on each trade. Traders often risk a small percentage of their account, such as 1% or 2%, on a single trade.

4. Risk Reward

Good trades often have a favorable risk-to-reward ratio. If you risk 50 pips to make 150 pips, your setup may be worth considering.

Quick Review Questions

  1. What is a stop loss used for? Answer: To limit losses.
  2. Why is position sizing important? Answer: It helps control the amount you risk.

Key Takeaways: Risk management protects your capital, stop losses limit losses, and position sizing keeps your account safe.

title: Trading Psychology
summary: Manage emotions and stick to your plan.
content:
Trading Psychology: Controlling Your Emotions

Type: Lesson

Duration: 4 minutes

Level: Intermediate

Lesson Objective

By the end of this lesson, you will understand:

  • How emotions affect trading
  • Why discipline matters
  • How to avoid revenge trading

1. Emotions in Trading

Fear and greed often cause traders to make poor decisions. A calm mind helps you follow your plan instead of reacting to every price move.

2. Discipline

Discipline means following your strategy even when the market is noisy. It helps you avoid impulsive entries and exits.

3. Revenge Trading

Revenge trading happens when a trader tries to win back losses quickly. This often leads to more losses and poor risk management.

Quick Review Questions

  1. What emotion often leads to panic selling? Answer: Fear.
  2. What is revenge trading? Answer: Trying to recover losses too quickly.

Key Takeaways: Trading psychology is about staying calm, disciplined, and patient while following your plan.

title: Technical Setup
summary: Identify trend, support, and resistance on charts.
content:
Technical Setup: Reading the Market

Type: Lesson

Duration: 5 minutes

Level: Intermediate

Lesson Objective

By the end of this lesson, you will understand:

  • What trend, support, and resistance are
  • How to spot simple chart patterns
  • How to build a trading setup

1. Trend

A trend shows the general direction of price movement. An uptrend has higher highs and higher lows, while a downtrend has lower highs and lower lows.

2. Support and Resistance

Support is a price level where buying interest may appear. Resistance is a level where selling pressure may increase. These levels help traders find trade areas.

3. Building a Setup

A simple technical setup could include trend direction, a support or resistance zone, and a clear entry trigger. This helps remove guesswork from trading.

Quick Review Questions

  1. What is support? Answer: A level where price may find buying interest.
  2. What is resistance? Answer: A level where price may face selling pressure.

Key Takeaways: Technical analysis helps traders understand price behavior and identify potential entries and exits.

title: Breakout Strategy
summary: Learn how to trade breakout opportunities safely.
content:
Breakout Strategy: Trading the Move

Type: Lesson

Duration: 5 minutes

Level: Intermediate

Lesson Objective

By the end of this lesson, you will understand:

  • What a breakout is
  • How to wait for confirmation
  • How to manage breakout trades safely

1. What Is a Breakout?

A breakout happens when price moves beyond an important level such as support, resistance, or a consolidation range. Breakouts can signal the start of a strong move.

2. Why Confirmation Matters

Not every breakout continues. Confirmation could come from price closing above resistance or a strong momentum candle. This helps reduce fake breakouts.

3. Risk Management

Breakout traders often use stop losses below the breakout level and aim for a target based on the size of the range or a clear reward goal.

Quick Review Questions

  1. What is a breakout? Answer: A move beyond a key level.
  2. Why is confirmation important? Answer: It helps avoid false breakouts.

Key Takeaways: Breakouts can offer strong opportunities, but confirmation and risk control are essential.

title: Trend Following
summary: Follow momentum and keep trades aligned with the trend.
content:
Trend Following: Riding the Market Direction

Type: Lesson

Duration: 6 minutes

Level: Intermediate

Lesson Objective

By the end of this lesson, you will understand:

  • What trend following means
  • How to identify trend strength
  • How to stay aligned with momentum

1. What Is Trend Following?

Trend following means trading in the direction of the current market momentum. Traders look for persistent movement rather than trying to predict every turn.

2. Identifying a Trend

A trend can be seen through higher highs and higher lows in an uptrend, or lower highs and lower lows in a downtrend. Moving averages and price structure can help confirm momentum.

3. Staying With the Trend

One of the hardest parts of trend following is avoiding early exits. Patience and discipline help traders stay with a move long enough to capture momentum.

Quick Review Questions

  1. What is trend following? Answer: Trading in the direction of momentum.
  2. How can you spot a trend? Answer: By looking at higher highs and higher lows or lower highs and lower lows.

Key Takeaways: Trend following works best when you respect the market direction, not your own emotional reactions.

title: Fundamental News
summary: See how economic reports affect Forex prices.
content:
Fundamental News: What Drives Forex Moves

Type: Lesson

Duration: 4 minutes

Level: Intermediate

Lesson Objective

By the end of this lesson, you will understand:

  • How economic news affects Forex
  • Which reports matter most
  • How to trade around major events

1. Why News Matters

Economic releases such as CPI, employment data, and central bank decisions can cause sharp moves in currency prices. Traders often watch the news calendar closely.

2. Important Reports

Reports like interest rate decisions, inflation data, and employment numbers can change expectations for a currency. These changes often affect sentiment and momentum.

3. Trading Around News

Some traders avoid major news because of volatility, while others look for setups after the initial move. Either way, awareness of upcoming events is critical.

Quick Review Questions

  1. Why does economic news matter in Forex? Answer: It changes expectations and price direction.
  2. What kind of reports often move the market? Answer: Inflation, employment, and central bank announcements.

Key Takeaways: Fundamental news can cause strong market moves, so understanding the calendar helps you trade with more awareness.
